housingMarkets.evidenceSummary: Canada's housing crisis is structural and multi-year. Federal immigration targets of 400,000-500,000 annual newcomers clashed with construction capacity of 200,000-220,000 new units per year. Government announced international student cap in 2024 reducing study permit approvals by 35%. Despite this, the housing deficit accumulated over 2018-2025 will not resolve before 2030. Toronto and Vancouver are the worst affected. Montreal and Calgary remain viable. Federal housing plan aims to build 3.87 million new homes by 2031 but construction labor shortages threaten delivery.

housingMarkets.evidenceSummary: The Netherlands faces one of Europe's most acute student housing crises. Multiple Dutch universities (University of Amsterdam, Radboud, Maastricht) temporarily paused international student recruitment specifically citing housing inability. Vacancy rates nationally below 1%. The Dutch government's Housing Minister declared housing shortage of 390,000 units in 2025. Social housing waitlists in Amsterdam average 12-15 years. Private rental market liberalization (Wet Betaalbare Huur 2024) created new rent control rules but also caused many landlords to exit student market.

housingMarkets.housingCrisisLevel: SEVERE in Paris; MODERATE in Lyon/Grenoble/Toulouse; MANAGEABLE in smaller university cities
housingMarkets.evidenceSummary: France has a dual housing market: Paris faces a critical shortage with vacancy rates below 1% and rent inflation that has outpaced salary growth for a decade, while provincial university cities remain significantly more affordable. The CROUS (Centre Régional des Oeuvres Universitaires et Scolaires) student housing system provides subsidized accommodation but waitlists are long and supply severely insufficient. The CAF (Caisse d'Allocations Familiales) housing benefit (APL) partially subsidizes rent for low-income students and is accessible to international students with long-stay visa. France's Encadrement des loyers (rent control) in Paris and some other cities helps moderate private market rent growth but has not solved the structural shortage.

housingMarkets.evidenceSummary: The UAE real estate market, particularly Dubai, experienced extraordinary rental inflation of 20-30% in 2022-2023 as global capital, COVID-delayed demand, and wealthy migrant influx converged. While pace has moderated to 8-12% annually in 2024-2026, prices remain dramatically elevated compared to pre-2022 levels. Abu Dhabi is somewhat more stable. The UAE has no rent control equivalent in Dubai (DLD rules limit annual increase based on RERA index but enforcement complex). Sharjah has stricter rent control. For students, the MBZUAI scholarship model (which covers accommodation) is the only financially viable pathway. For professionals, company housing allowance is a critical negotiation component. Zero income tax means high gross salaries but housing consumes significant portion of net income.

housingMarkets.recommendation: UAE housing strategy for Bangladeshi AI students and professionals: (1) MBZUAI scholarship is the ONLY financially viable student path - private market is prohibitively expensive without institutional support. (2) For post-graduation employment, negotiate housing allowance as non-negotiable part of offer before accepting. (3) Live in Sharjah or International City/JVC in Dubai to maximize savings. (4) Join Bangladeshi UAE community networks immediately upon arrival - housing referrals through community are most reliable. (5) Use UAE's zero-tax salary advantage and low housing (via community sharing) to maximize savings for 5-7 years. (6) Exit to settlement-friendly country (Canada, Australia, Germany) with substantial capital for property purchase and family establishment. UAE is wealth accumulation phase; not final destination.
